verdict.rationale: Luma's own materials say video generation supports character reference and keyframes, and that style references, character references and visual grounding are carried into every asset so a brand or character holds steady across outputs. Character consistency is also claimed for expression transfer. These are first-party marketing-level claims only, with no detailed docs on how references persist across separate shots and no hands-on confirmation. The community complaint about morphing and weak temporal coherence concerns quality within a single clip, so it is not a concrete counter-example to cross-shot consistency. Missing for 10: detailed documentation of the cross-shot character/scene reference workflow, independent or hands-on corroboration of consistency across multiple generations, and evidence for scene (not just character) consistency across shots.
